notices.html: Apple picking is still spotty after the spring freeze: Battleview has no apples at all this year, and Johnson's Corner Farm lost about 80% of its crop. Terhune's apple status remains unclear, so call ahead if apples are the main reason for your trip.
Polar Express train rides are filling up for late November and December: Whippany and Phillipsburg both have 2026 dates on sale now, and popular weekends sell out early.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend: Fall Family Fun Weekends continues both days, with free wagon rides 11am to 3pm and live music 12 to 4pm, plus the corn maze, hay-bale maze, barnyard and pumpkin picking. Advance tickets are required for festival entry, reported anywhere from about $10 to $14 per person online. Apple status is still unclear this fall, the orchard manager said in spring that most of the crop was likely lost, so call 609-924-2310 to check both before you go.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: pick-your-own pumpkins should still be going, open Mon to Sat 9am to 6pm and Sun 2 to 6pm, with a corn maze and hayrides. Apple supply is still uncertain after this spring's regionwide freeze, so call 609-448-0629 to check what's actually ripe before you drive over.
blurbs.vonthun: This weekend likely falls in Von Thun's Fall Festival Weekends, with one admission price covering the hayride, corn maze and farm animals, while pumpkin and apple picking cost extra. We couldn't confirm this week's exact hours, ticket price or apple availability, so call 732-329-8656 to check before you go.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: the farm should be open with pick-your-own pumpkins, a corn maze, hayrides and farm animals, plus the pie counter that's the real reason to go. Emery's is mainly a berry farm so the spring apple freeze shouldn't affect your visit here, but call 609-758-8514 to confirm hours since we couldn't verify them this week.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: still no apple picking, the April freeze wiped out Battleview's entire crop this year, but pumpkin picking (priced by weight, cash only) and the sunflower field continue. The country store is open 9am to 5pm daily except Tuesdays. Call 732-462-0756 or check their Facebook page to confirm picking hours before you go.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: the Harvest Festival should continue with the corn maze, hayrides, gem mining, a petting zoo and pick-your-own pumpkins and gourds. The farm lost about 80% of its apple crop to the spring freeze, so expect apples to be very limited if available at all. Call 609-654-8643 to check before planning on apples specifically.
blurbs.dinosafari: This weekend: still closed for the season, since it only ran July 1 through August 16. It's expected to return next summer, so there's no need for a special trip until then.
blurbs.sixflags: This weekend: Fright Fest is running, daytime rides are fine for kids 9 to 10, but evening haunted mazes and scare zones start around 6pm and lean older. Plan an earlier visit and head out before dark if that's a concern.
blurbs.diggerland: This weekend: Diggerfest continues through mid November, included with general admission, with weekend-only rides plus Dig or Treat trick-or-treating and a costume parade on select dates. The park runs weekends only this time of year, so Saturday and Sunday are your options.
blurbs.sesame: This weekend: The Count's Halloween Spooktacular continues on select dates through November 1 with trick-or-treating, a parade, dance parties and a scarecrow scavenger hunt. Hours vary by day, so check before you go.
blurbs.lsc: This weekend: the Jennifer Chalsty Planetarium is running regular weekend hours, 10am to 5pm, still the biggest planetarium in the hemisphere. Book timed tickets online first.
